title: Segmented KV striping and heuristic eviction for hybrid tensor/pipeline parallel
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Background: On multi-GPU hosts with mixed tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) topologies, the KV cache becomes a significant memory pressure point. Existing monolithic KV allocations or blunt sharding strategies produce hotspots, cross-GPU fragmentation, and unnecessary host<->device transfers for sliding-window workloads.

Problem: We need a memory-efficient scheme that: 1) reduces peak GPU memory for KV state across TP/PP layouts, 2) limits cross-device synchronization during continuous batching, 3) supports fast eviction for long context sessions without impacting latency SLOs, and 4) is compatible with runtime fallback policies and quantized model variants.
proposal_summary: Introduce segmented KV striping with a local shadow mirror and a lightweight heuristic eviction layer. The runtime will split KV storage into fixed-size segments striped across GPUs according to a topology-aware mapping. Each GPU keeps a compact local shadow index and a small MRU hot segment set. Eviction uses a two-tier heuristic: segment-level aging + prefix reuse score. For pipeline stages that require contiguous prefix access, we implement transient replication for affected segments to avoid synchronous cross-GPU fetch during critical low-latency paths.
design_details: Segmenting: Break the logical KV cache into 64KB segments (configurable). Each segment contains contiguous key/value pairs for a token range and is the unit of placement and eviction.

Topology-aware striping: Use a placement function that considers TP/PP mapping and intra-host NVLink/PCIe topology to minimize cross-host traffic. Default: round-robin across GPUs within the same NVLink domain, then to other domains as needed.
Local shadow index: Each GPU stores a compact bloom-filter-like index (64-256 bytes per segment) plus MRU list for hot segments. The index allows fast negative lookups without RPCs.

Transient replication: If a request's decode window spans segments located on different pipeline stages, transiently replicate up to 2 adjacent segments to the requesting stage's GPU(s) for the duration of the decode. Replication occurs asynchronously and is bounded by a replication budget per request.

Heuristic eviction: Two-stage policy: 1) coarse segment aging (time since last access), 2) prefix reuse score computed from recent request traces (weights recent prefix hits higher). Eviction operates at segment granularity to keep memcpy and allocation overheads low.

Continuous batching interactions: Batch scheduler will consider segment locality when coalescing requests to favor batches that touch overlapping segment sets. A locality score augments the scheduler cost function.

Compatibility: Works with quantized KV representations by storing quantized values inside segments and maintaining separate metadata for scale/zero points. Compatible with existing cache persistence and checkpoint formats with a migration tool.
Config knobs: segment_size, replication_budget_per_request, local_index_size, eviction_age_threshold, locality_weight_in_scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end rollout on staging for a 4xA100 host with 2-way TP and 3 PP stages without regressions to base latency SLO (99th <= baseline+10ms) for our chat streaming benchmark.
Peak GPU memory for KV reduced by >=18% on average for long-context workloads (>8k tokens) compared to current slab approach.
Eviction correctness: no stale-KV correctness bugs observed across 1000 fuzzed sessions; unit tests for segment rehydration and replication pass.
Metrics and traces show reduction in cross-GPU synchronous fetches during decoding by >=40%.
Migration tool can convert existing on-disk KV snapshots to segmented format within bounded time (<=30s for typical 8GB snapshots on CI host).
implementation_steps: 1) Add segmented KV storage layer and on-disk format (storage adapter + migration tool).
2) Implement local shadow index and MRU microcache on GPU-side allocator.
3) Implement topology-aware placement function using node/PCIe/NVLink graph.
4) Add transient replication protocol with async memcpy and bounded replication budget.
5) Hook segment locality into continuous batch scheduler cost model.
6) Implement heuristic eviction and safe reclamation path (grace period for in-flight decodes).
7) Add observability: per-segment metrics, replication counts, shadow-index misses, eviction events.
8) End-to-end testing on staging, rollout to canary hosts, monitor for regressions.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature branch + unit tests; internal dogfood on small cluster (2 hosts).
Stage 1: Staging rollout on 4xA100 single host topology for regression testing. Run synthetic long-context generation and chat streaming suites overnight.
Stage 2: Canary rollout to 5% of production hosts, restrict to non-critical customers, monitor KPIs for 48h. Auto-rollback if latency_p99 regresses >10% or error rate increases >0.2%.
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% with continuous telemetry for one week, adjust eviction params.
Stage 4: Global rollout and mark runtime-1.22 as supporting segmented KV. Publish migration steps for Dedicated/Private customers.
test_plan: Unit tests: segment allocation/free, index negative-lookups, replication budget enforcement.
Integration: simulate TP/PP topologies with synthetic requests that exercise cross-stage prefixes and verify correctness under eviction load.
Load: long-context (16k tokens) continuous batching workload to measure memory and latency impact.
Fuzz: interleave evictions, migrations, and checkpoint restore to detect race conditions.
Compatibility: verify conversion tool against 3 historical KV snapshot formats.
Performance: compare against baseline slab allocator on standard benchmarks (latency and throughput).
monitoring_alerts: Alert: kv_cross_gpu_sync_count rate > baseline*0.6 for 5m => investigate placement/regression.
Alert: KV_peak_gpu_memory_bytes > host_limit - 2GB => trigger eviction aggressiveness increase and pagedump.
Alert: kv_evictions_per_minute spikes by >3x => possible workload shift; flag for PM review.
Alert: segment_replication_ops/second > replication_budget_threshold => throttle replications and log affected requests.
Dashboard: per-host KV heatmap with segment ownership and replication traces.
SLO: latency_decode_p99 must remain within +10ms of baseline during canary.
open_questions: What is the optimal default segment_size for GPUs with different memory hierarchies (A100 40GB vs A100 80GB vs H100)?
Should transient replication be applied proactively for predicted prefix reuse or only reactively when a request spans remote segments?
How do we reconcile replication budget with fairness across concurrent requests from different customers? (per-request vs per-host budgeting)
Edge case: how to safely evict segments referenced by long-running decoding with preemptible GPUs?
Instrumentation: what is the acceptable overhead of the local shadow index on tiny/embedded GPUs?
comments: 2025-02-12 Sana Patel: Initial spike showed ~22% memory improvement in synthetic long context when using 64KB segments on a 4-GPU host. Observed a small increase in replication traffic but negligible added latency in non-contended runs.

2025-02-18 Luca Moretti: Implemented prototype of local shadow index. Bloom-filter false positive rate tuned to 1% yields best trade-off between extra replication and index size. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1289
2025-02-24 Design review (Marta Chen): Agreed on topology-aware placement; asked for clear telemetry to show NVLink/PCIe hop counts. Action: add per-replication hop trace.
2025-03-01 Infra (Jamal Ortiz): We need to expose PCI graph in the node agent for placement decisions. Added dependency on INFRA-402.
2025-03-03 QA (Priya Rao): Found a race when eviction reclaims a replicated segment while async memcpy still in-flight. Mitigation: add grace-window and in-flight refcounts.
